video:video.video:title: Michael Jordan Was Left Off the List. Here's Where He Began.
video:video.video:description: In 1978, a 15-year-old sophomore at Laney High School in Wilmington, North Carolina walked up to the varsity list. His name wasn't on it. Twenty years later he hit the most famous shot in NBA history.

video:video.video:title: Elon Musk Had One Launch Left. Here's Where He Began.
video:video.video:description: In 2008, Elon Musk was zero for three. Three Falcon 1 rockets had failed, Tesla was running out of money, and he had one launch left. This is where he began: the boy in South Africa who taught himself to code, the bullying, PayPal, the bet on SpaceX, Christmas Eve 2008, and the rocket that finally reached orbit.

video:video.video:title: Lionel Messi: At 39 He Said Goodbye. At 10, He'd Almost Stopped Growing.
video:video.video:description: At 39, in front of 85,000 phones at the Monumental, Lionel Messi said goodbye to Argentina. At 10, he was the smallest boy on every team in Rosario, and his body had almost stopped growing.

video:video.video:title: Cristiano Ronaldo's Heart Almost Ended It at 15
video:video.video:description: Turin, April 2018. Cristiano Ronaldo, 33, back to goal, and Juventus fans stand up for the man beating them.

video:video.video:title: Kobe Bryant Airballed Four Times at Eighteen
video:video.video:description: May 12, 1997. Kobe Bryant is eighteen, and in one playoff night in Salt Lake City he shoots four airballs. The building laughs. That night he goes looking for a gym.

video:video.video:title: NVIDIA Had Thirty Days of Cash
video:video.video:description: NVIDIA has about thirty days of cash. In a Japan conference room in the mid-1990s, Jensen Huang asks Sega’s Shoichiro Irimajiri for about five million dollars — and tells him the money will most likely be lost.

video:video.video:title: Apple Fired Steve Jobs at Thirty
video:video.video:description: Apple's board fires Steve Jobs at thirty. A chairman's title that runs nothing. Then a resignation dated September 17, 1985.

video:video.video:title: WhatsApp: The Line That Didn't Work
video:video.video:description: He almost shut it down. Food stamps. A dead landline in Fastiv. Then a dollar-a-year app that refused ads — and a nineteen-billion-dollar check on a welfare-office door.

video:video.video:title: Phil Knight: The Frozen Account and the Trunk
video:video.video:description: The Bank of California has frozen the account. A runner who keeps books is one lawsuit and one bank from ruin.

video:video.video:title: Rolex: The Orphan Who Put a Watch on the Wrist
video:video.video:description: In 1905 a man's wristwatch was still a joke. A Bavarian importer bet a partnership on it anyway.
